question.text: A potentiometer wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>32</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is connected in series with a battery of EMF <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, internal resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> and external resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>. If a secondary cell of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is balanced at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length. Then value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Potential gradient of potentiometer=2.5(3+R+32)×3010
Balancing length for cell of emf e=0.4 V is 8 cm.
∴2.5(35+R)×3×8=0.4
⇒5×3×4=0.04×(35+R)10
⇒15×10=35+R
⇒R=115 Ω
